Photograph: Anadolu/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Edward Zimbardi allegedly skipped his son’s wedding in Virginia after correctly suspecting FBI agents might try to arrest him. Photograph: Anadolu/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images US crime Georgia man deported from Fiji to face $165m crypto Ponzi scheme charges Edward Zimbardi, 59, who had fled US, will appear in court in Los Angeles on wire fraud and money-laundering charges Reuters Tue 18 Aug 2026 08.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A man from Flowery Branch, Georgia , has been deported from Fiji to face charges in his home state accusing him of defrauding more than 6,000 investors and causing more than $165m of losses in ⁠a cryptocurrency Ponzi ⁠scheme, the ​US attorney in Atlanta said on Monday. Edward Zimbardi, 59, was indicted on 12 counts of ⁠wire fraud, 12 counts of money laundering and one count of money-laundering conspiracy. Prosecutors said Zimbardi pitched The ⁠Crypto Program as a means to purchase online advertising packages, offering a guaranteed 25% ​monthly rate of return on ‌an initial $550 investment. However, instead ‌of buying advertising packages, Zimbardi allegedly lost tens of millions of dollars betting ‌on foreign currency and spent at least $10m on personal expenses, including a house for one of his sons and alimony payments). He also purportedly used new money to repay earlier investors. Prosecutors said the alleged scheme ran from June 2022 to August 2023. They said Zimbardi fled to Fiji ‌in July 2025 after learning that the FBI was scrutinizing him – and that he skipped the May wedding of one of his sons ​in Virginia after correctly suspecting that agents might try to arrest him. Investigators traveled to Fiji to escort him back to the US, arriving in Los Angeles . “He had victims all over the world,” US attorney Theodore Hertzberg in Atlanta ⁠said at a news conference. “If you’re promised 25% returns every month ​by somebody who expresses ​remorse for having ‘accidentally’ lost your ​money in the past, you might be willing to go ​with it ‌because you’re that desperate ​to get ​your money back.” Zimbardi was expected to make an initial appearance in Los Angeles federal court. A federal public defender representing him there did not immediately respond to a request for comment. New tapes reveal what may have sparked Sharon Tate murders Sep 5, 2026 | 6:00 AM For decades, the prevailing story of the Manson murders held that Charles Manson masterminded a murderous plot to ignite a race war inspired by the Beatles. But Joe Berlinger argues the infamous story never added up. The true crime filmmaker directed a three-part Netflix docuseries titled “Conversations with a Killer: The Charles Manson Tapes.” It features previously unreleased prison audio from the cult leader and some of his “Manson Family” members. In 1969, the career criminal who surrounded himself with runaways and other lost souls directed his followers to commit a series of murders in and around Los Angeles. Prosecutors argued the killings were part of Manson’s “Helter Skelter” plan to ignite a race war. CHARLES MANSON’S GRANDDAUGHTER REVEALS MOMENT SHE DISCOVERED DARK FAMILY SECRET: ‘IT WAS DEVASTATING’ But after studying the previously unreleased recordings, Berlinger argues the murders were instead a desperate attempt to cover up “a series of blunders.” “This whole idea of starting a race war was a false idea,” Berlinger told Fox News Digital. “He certainly believed a race war was coming, or at least that’s what he told his followers to control them. But the murders, in particular the Tate and LaBianca murders , were an attempt to get associate Bobby Beausoleil out of prison. He told his followers, ‘He’s my friend. You guys owe me a favor. Let’s get him out of prison.'” “The truth is I believe, and others believe, that if they had succeeded in this crazy idea of getting Bobby Beausoleil out of prison, I think Manson would’ve killed him because he was a liability,” said Berlinger. “But listening to those tapes made the story come alive, not these crazy conspiracy theories and myths that turned Charles Manson into the most mythologized figure in the history of true crime .” Berlinger traces the chain of events that led to the murders to a botched drug deal. According to the documentary , Manson invited members of the Straight Satans motorcycle club to Spahn Ranch to protect him from the Black Panthers, whom he feared, offering them access to his female followers in exchange. “[Follower] Tex Watson tried to steal money from a drug dealer named Bernard ‘Lotsapoppa’ Crowe, who wants his money back,” Berlinger explained. “Manson goes out there and doesn’t intend to kill him, but thinks he killed him, a Black Panther.” FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X According to the documentary, Watson stole Crowe’s money, prompting Crowe to threaten retaliation. Manson later shot Crowe and mistakenly believed he had killed him. Crowe was not a Black Panther. “He goes back to Spahn Ranch and becomes paranoid that the Black Panthers are going to come after him. He becomes friends with Bobby, tells him to join the family and also to help protect the ranch. Bobby becomes tight with some bikers who were also invited to protect the ranch from the Black Panthers.” But the motorcycle gang wanted more than just women. The documentary says Beausoleil brought them drugs he obtained from music teacher Gary Hinman. The bikers were unhappy with the quality of the supply, and Beausoleil was pressured to recover their money. “Bobby tries to get his money back from Gary and can’t get it,” said Berlinger. According to court records, during the confrontation, Manson arrived at Hinman’s home and slashed Hinman’s face with a sword, cutting him from his left ear toward his chin. Over the course of about three days, Manson’s followers tortured Hinman. Beausoleil later stabbed Hinman to death and wrote the words “Political Piggy” on a wall in Hinman’s blood, along with an animal paw print intended to implicate the Black Panthers. “Gary Hinman is killed because Manson comes in, wields a sword and then tells Bobby ‘finish the job’ to cover the tracks,” Berlinger said. SIGN UP TO GET THE TRUE CRIME NEWSLETTER Beausoleil was arrested about a week after Hinman’s body was discovered. Berlinger said Beausoleil was driving Hinman’s vehicle and had “the murder weapon stupidly in the stolen car.” Berlinger said Manson wanted police to believe Hinman’s murder was the work of the Black Panthers to cast suspicion away from Beausoleil. He noted the attempt to free Beausoleil became the catalyst for the murders that followed. On Aug. 9, 1969, Manson’s followers murdered five people at a Los Angeles home previously rented by music producer Terry Melcher: actress Sharon Tate, who was 8 1/2 months pregnant; coffee heiress Abigail Folger; celebrity hairstylist Jay Sebring; Polish writer Wojciech Frykowski; and Steven Parent, who had been visiting the estate’s caretaker. Melcher had previously declined to sign Manson to a recording contract. “The murder is tried to be made to look like it was part of Gary Hinman’s murder ,” said Berlinger. “But when Manson picks up the paper the next day, and there’s no information about these two murders being linked, they do another murder. The logic is, ‘We’ve got to make people think that Bobby, who is sitting in prison, is not guilty.’” “This was all a series of blunders, a bunch of bad, spontaneous decision-making.” GET REAL-TIME UPDATES DIRECTLY ON THE TRUE CRIME HUB The next night, wealthy grocer Leno LaBianca and his wife, Rosemary LaBianca, were stabbed and killed in their home across town. The killers scrawled phrases including “Pigs” and the misspelled words “Healter Skelter” in blood at the crime scene. Manson was arrested in October 1969. Prosecutors maintained at trial that Manson ordered his followers to kill some of Los Angeles’ rich and famous to trigger a race war, a plan prosecutors said grew in part from his interpretation of the Beatles’ song “Helter Skelter.” Manson frequently spoke about an impending race war and interpreted songs on the Beatles’ “White Album” as messages about the coming conflict, according to testimony from his followers. What remains disputed is whether those beliefs motivated the Tate-LaBianca murders or whether, as Berlinger argues, prosecutors elevated them into the central theory of their case. “[Prosecutor Vincent Bugliosi] had to come up with a legal theory to convict a guy who actually didn’t do the killings,” Berlinger said. “Manson wasn’t even there when the Tate-LaBianca killings took place. So how do you convict somebody who wasn’t there? Well, you come up with this organizing principle that he convinced his followers that a race war was coming, and he was trying to make that race war happen. It was a brilliant legal theory, but it’s a false story.” “The Manson murders are much more tragic, but much more banal than this idea of some crazy cult trying to start a race war,” Berlinger continued. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS “This was a drug deal gone bad, trying to cover up Gary Hinman’s killing by doing another murder the next day to make it look like a copycat murder, which were the Tate murders. And when that murder didn’t hit newspapers like a Black Panther murder, they did the LaBianca murders. It’s a series of blunders by people who were trying to cover their tracks, not this grand scheme of ‘Helter Skelter.'” GOT A TIP? Bugliosi worked with writer Curt Gentry on a book about the case. Published in 1974, “Helter Skelter” became the bestselling true crime book of all time. Manson and three followers — Susan Atkins, Patricia Krenwinkel and Leslie Van Houten — were found guilty and later sentenced to death. Charles “Tex” Watson was tried separately and convicted later. Their death sentences were reduced to life in prison after the California Supreme Court invalidated the state’s death penalty in 1972. Atkins died in prison in 2009. Van Houten was released on parole in 2023. Krenwinkel and Watson remain in prison. LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? https://www.azernews.az/region/263442.ht.text: Latvia, Lithuania weigh ban on Russian grain transit amid rising shipments 6 September 2026 08:00 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more Latvia and Lithuania are considering suspending the transit of Russian grain through their ports amid a sharp increase in shipments following Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia’s export infrastructure. According to sources familiar with the matter, Russia has begun redirecting grain exports to ports in the Baltic states after Ukrainian drone attacks disrupted other routes. Shipment volumes could rise sharply in October, the sources said. The Latvian government plans to discuss a complete ban on such transit routes, according to the report. Lithuanian authorities, meanwhile, have not yet announced specific restrictions. Lithuanian Prime Minister Sinkyavičius said that exporting Russian grain through Lithuania’s infrastructure was inconsistent with the country’s values. The potential restrictions come as Baltic countries continue to reassess their economic ties with Russia amid the ongoing war in Ukraine. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c83v.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The Northern Bridge is the second major bridge to be targeted by Russia in recent days, Kyiv's mayor said By Ella Kipling Published 3 October 2026, 07:13 BST Updated 1 hour ago A Russian strike has hit a second major bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko has said, as Russia ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital. The attack on Saturday morning damaged the road surface and trolleybus overhead wires on the Northern (Pivnichnyi) Bridge, Klitschko said, causing traffic to be blocked. The strike comes after another key bridge in the city, Southern (Pivdennyi) Bridge, was targeted multiple times by Russian drones on Thursday and Friday, with Klitschko earlier warning that such attacks were "tearing Kyiv apart" . The Northern and Southern bridges link the eastern and western parts of the capital and had not been hit before Thursday, signalling a new stage in Moscow's strategy. Attacks on the Southern Bridge have caused major travel disruption since Thursday, with metro and car travel across it suspended. Many of the city's residents - which number about three million - rely on the metro to travel across the city. Image source, Reuters Image caption, In the Thursday attack, a Russian drone hit cables of Kyiv's Pivdennyi bridge Writing on Telegram on Saturday, Klitschko said: "Hitting the North Bridge. Emergency services are on their way." "Traffic on the bridge from the left to the right bank is currently blocked," he added. Russia's defence ministry said it had hit the bridge, saying it was used for military troop transfers and logistics. It also said it targeted a logistics centre in the city. Klitschko did not mention this. Earlier attacks on the Southern Bridge prompted Kyiv's defence council to hold a crisis meeting on Friday, prompting Klitschko to warn afterwards that the city was now in a "very dramatic situation" as Moscow was battering its "critical infrastructure, logistics, housing" and other key facilities. Russian President Vladimir Putin has said Russia is acting in response to Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy facilities, despite the fact that it was Moscow that had first launched such attacks. Image source, Reuters/State Emergency Service of Ukraine Image caption, Strikes on the Southern Bridge caused major traffic delays across the city After the Southern Bridge was attacked, passengers described how dust from a blast wave entered their carriage through the ventilation system. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Putin had decided that there were "no rules now" when attacking Ukraine. In an interview with the Financial Times, he said: "The Russians have failed to occupy us. So now they are carrying out massive attacks and mass killings." He added: "They want to destroy our bridges... our data centres, the internet, mobile networks, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, universities - everything. They want people to flee their cities." Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
